annotations.annotation_text: Page 181 opens Book 1, Chapter 7 ("Shem the Penman") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions, featuring Shem, Shaun (as Justius), ALP (Mercius). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "Letter" on page 181 ("Shem the Penman"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. During this Age of Gods phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 181 ("Shem the Penman"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
